In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the cationic rare earth metal complex-catalyzed cis-1, 4-polymerizations of butadiene and isoprene.
the mechanism of cis-1, 4-polymerisation of butadiene, catalysed by cationic rare earth metal complex bearing an anciillary PNP ligands.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regio- and stereo-selectivity of butadiene insertion into the metal-alkyl bond is determined by the electronic and steric properties of the central metal and ancillary ligands.

the electronic factor of the metal center and the steric effect of the ancillary ligand have a decisive influence on both regioselectivity and cis- vs. tran-selectivity of the insertion of diene monomer into the metal–allyl bond.
the cis- vs. trans-insertion and regioselectivity of monomer insertion are mainly determined by the electronic and steric effects of central metal and monomer respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rare-earth metal complex with the PNP ligand has a high cis-1, 4-selectivity for the polymerization of dienes.

a rare-earth metal cationic complex bearing the ancillary PNP-ligand is capable of catalyzing the cis-1, 4-polymerizations of dienes with a high regioselectivity, and the chain growth follows the allyl-insertion mechanism.
the cis- vs trans-insertion is mainly determined by the central metal and the regio-selectivity is predominantly controlled by steric hindrances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cis- vs trans-selectivity is mainly controlled by the central metal, whereas the regio-selectivity is mainly determined by the ancillary ligand.

the cis- vs.trans- and cis-1, 4-vs.-1, 2-selectivity of butadiene insertion is mainly governed by the steric hindrance around the metal center, and the electronic factor of the metal center is of less importance.

the rare-earth metal complexes bearing PNP ligand can be used as efficient and selective catalysts for cis-1, 4-polymerizations of conjugated dienes, which is in line with the experimental observations.
